# `Q-5-17` — Unknown project type

> `_quarto.yml` sets a `project.type` that is neither built-in nor
> contributed by an installed extension; the render stops.

## What this means

`project.type` decides how every document in the project is processed.
Quarto resolves it against two sources: the built-in types
(`default`, `website`, `book`, `manuscript`) and the types contributed
by extensions in `_extensions/` via `contributes: project:`.

When neither matches — or when the value is not a string at all — the
render stops before any document is processed.

Stopping is deliberate. Earlier Quarto 2 versions continued with
default-project behavior, and that turned out to be the worse failure:
a broken site build looks like a successful one, and every document
gets its own copy of the shared JS and CSS written next to the source
file, littering the tree. An error at the start is easier to act on
than a scattered mess at the end.

## Why this happens

- **A typo in the type name.**
- **An extension that is not installed** in this project. Extensions
  are per-project; one installed elsewhere is not visible here.
- **An extension whose manifest failed to load.** This is the cause
  worth checking first — look for a
  [`Q-16-1`](../extension/Q-16-1.qmd) warning alongside this error. A
  broken `_extension.yml` means the extension contributes nothing, and
  its project type becomes unknown.
- **A non-string value**, such as a list or a mapping, usually from
  YAML indentation that nested more than intended.

## How to fix

The error's hints list the project-contributing extensions Quarto did
find, which is the fastest way to spot a near-miss in the name.

For a built-in type, use one of the four:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
```

For an extension type, install it and use the full
`organization/name` form:

```bash
quarto add <owner>/<repo>
```

```yaml
project:
  type: my-org/docs
```

If a `Q-16-1` was reported next to this error, fix that manifest first
— this error usually goes with it.
